messages.subject: MCDS - abundance estimation with effort
parts:
Hello, 

I am a little confused with coding to estimate abundance with MCDS including effort. I did a little search but I don't find any answers, so I am writing here.

I have a data sheet with all the detections and for each one,  the Area, Region.Label, Sample.Label and Effort was defined. 

I have another datasheet for the effort which include all the transects surveyed with Area, Region.Label and Sample.Label. I created a table 'Region.table' with two colums: Region.Label and Area and another table 'Sample.table' with three columns: Region.Label, Sample.Label, Effort.

I have another datasheet for the effort that includes all the transects surveyed with Area, Region.Label and Sample.Label. I created from this a table 'Region.table' with two columns: Region.Label and Area and another table 'Sample.table' with three columns: Region.Label, Sample.Label, Effort.

To estimate abundance, I used this following code: 
Result<- ds(data, transect="line", key="hr", formula=~factor(SwellHeight), convert_units = conversion.factor, truncation=1500, region_table = Region.table, sample_table = Sample.table)

I got this warning message:
 Warning message:
In merge.data.frame(data, model$data, by.x = "object", by.y = "object", : column names ‘Region.Label.y’, ‘Sample.Label.y’ are duplicated in the result

I don't understand why I got this warning.
Maybe there is another way to estimate abundance?

I know that the total length of transects is 7127 km. In the summary of the model, I found 14306km which is not normal.

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: {Disarmed} Re: [distance-sampling] MCDS - abundance estimation with effort
parts:
Camille

As best I can make out, you're hybridising between the two data formats that ds​ understands.

Either use the flatfile​ format to have all information in a single data frame, or create three data frames containing information about the strata, transects and detections. From what I can tell, I think you need a data frame for the argument obs_table​ and then dispense with the data​ argument.  Here is the story from the documentation for ds​

Data format

One can supply data only to simply fit a detection function. However, if abundance/density estimates are necessary further information is required. Either the region_table, sample_table and obs_table data.frames can be supplied or all data can be supplied as a "flat file" in the data argument. In this format each row in data has additional information that would ordinarily be in the other tables. This usually means that there are additional columns named: Sample.Label, Region.Label, Effort and Area for each observation. See MailScanner has detected a possible fraud attempt from "127.0.0.1:10779" claiming to be flatfile for an example.
